title: fix(rest): the approvals, email, sharing, sharing-rule and analytics routes answer from the request's environment kernel when one REST plugin fronts many environments

_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPSQS59N7Px4367s49jMWcuS)_

_Keep one value on each of the two lines above, each line starting with its key.
[Human Minimum](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#human-minimum)
item 5 says what they mean._

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：一个 REST 插件挂在宿主内核前面、后面有多个环境内核时（云上托管运行时），审批、邮件、共享、共享规则、分析这五类接口改为到请求所属环境的内核里取服务，不再到宿主内核里取。
- 为什么改：宿主内核上没有这些服务，所以每个托管环境的审批中心列表都是空的、单条审批打开是 501，记录页的审批区也是空的，共享、共享规则和邮件接口一律 501（#29999）。
- 风险与回滚：只影响注册了 kernel-manager 的部署；单内核（社区版自部署）走原路，有测试钉住。分析接口在环境缺分析服务时不再借用宿主的分析服务，改为返回 501。回滚即 revert 本 PR，无配置或数据迁移。
- 先看：`packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts`（`environmentScopedProvider` 一段，风险在“不回退到宿主”那条腿）、`packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts`（删掉宿主回退的 `resolveService`）、`packages/rest/src/rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run src/rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts`，预期 1 个文件、58 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` builds the five provider seams it hands `RestServer` (`email`, `sharing`, `approvals`, `sharingRules`, `analytics`) from one factory, `environmentScopedProvider(slot)`. Each answers by these legs, in order:

- **An environment id and a registered `kernel-manager`**: read the slot on that environment's kernel, acquired with `kernelManager.getOrCreate(id)`, the same acquisition the data path's `resolveProtocol` makes. "Never registered" (the branded registry error) is `undefined`, and any other fault (a factory that threw) is re-raised, matching `objectQLProvider`'s three-state classification. There is no fallback to the plugin's own (host) occupant.
- **The reserved `platform` id, no id, or no `kernel-manager`**: `ctx.getService(slot)` on the plugin's own kernel, exactly as before.

The provider resolves no environment itself. Each route asks the one existing resolver, `RestServer.resolveRequestEnvironmentId(environmentId, req)`, and hands its answer to the provider:

- the scoped mount (`/environments/:environmentId/...`) answers the param;
- the unscoped (hostname-routed) mount answers through the host's `kernel-resolver` (`resolveEnvironment` first, so the id lookup buys no kernel), then the hostname / `X-Environment-Id` chain, as the data routes do.

Route-side, each moved route body's host interface gains `resolveRequestEnvironmentId` (typed as the class member), and `rest-server.ts` adds it to the host literals:

- `approvals-routes.ts`: `resolveService(environmentId, req)` at all 8 call sites.
- `sharing-routes.ts`: the same for the shares doors and the sharing-rule doors (8 call sites).
- `email-routes.ts`: `POST /email/send`.
- `record-page-routes.ts`: the approvals part of `POST /data/:object/:id/page`.
- `analytics-routes.ts`: `resolveService` keeps the shared resolver call it already made, drops its own inline `kernelManager` lookup (now the provider's) and drops the host fallback. `kernelManager` leaves `AnalyticsRouteHost` and the analytics host literal.

A changeset (`@objectstack/rest` patch) carries the same declaration lines.

## Why

On cloud's hosted runtime one `RestApiPlugin` sits on the host kernel in front of many environment kernels, and each environment registers these five services on its own kernel. The providers read `ctx.getService` on the host kernel whatever id they were handed, so the environment's services were never reached (#29999). The data routes never had this problem because they resolve the request's kernel; this change makes the five seams use that same resolution.

The reading per provider, as the card asked (step 2), measured by the hosted-shape test below against the base sources:

| Provider | Doors | Hosted shape before this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `approvals` | `GET /approvals/requests`, `GET /approvals/requests/:id` (and the lock, decide, recall and action doors on the same seam), record page approvals part | **Wrong.** Host-only read; the host carries no `approvals`, so the list answered `{ data: [] }`, a single request 501 and the record page part `{ requests: [], lock: null }`. |
| `sharing` | `/data/:object/:id/shares` | **Wrong.** Host-only read; the host mounts no sharing plugin, so 501. |
| `sharingRules` | `/sharing/rules/*` | **Wrong.** Same as `sharing` (the sharing plugin registers both slots on the environment kernel), so 501. |
| `email` | `POST /email/send` | **Wrong.** Host-only read; the host mounts no email plugin, so 501. |
| `analytics` | `POST /analytics/dataset/query` | **Right when the environment carries analytics** (the route already read the environment's kernel first), **wrong otherwise**: when the environment's kernel carried no analytics service, or could not be acquired, the route fell back to the host's provider instead of answering from the request's environment alone. |

## Tests

- **New** `packages/rest/src/rest-environment-scoped-providers.test.ts` (58). It boots real `ObjectKernel`s: a host kernel carrying the real `createRestApiPlugin` (scoping on, `projectResolution: 'auto'`), a `kernel-manager` double with the real manager's dedupe of concurrent builds and build / acquisition counters, a `kernel-resolver` mapping the `Host` header to an environment, and host-tagged occupants of all five slots. Behind it are three environment kernels: `env_alpha` and `env_beta` each carry auth, a protocol, an engine and their own tagged occupants of the five slots, and `env_bare` carries none of the five. Seven doors are driven through the real mounted handlers: approvals list, approvals get, shares list, sharing rules list, email send, the inline dataset query and the record page's approvals part.
  - **Isolation (the card's hard criterion):** every door × {scoped, hostname} × {A, B} answers 200 with the target environment's row, and exactly one downstream call is recorded, the target's: none from the host, none from the other environment (28 cases).
  - **No host fallback:** every door × {scoped, hostname} for `env_bare` gets the door's own absent answer (`{ data: [] }` for the list, `{ requests: [], lock: null }` for the record page part, 501 elsewhere) and reaches no occupant at all (14 cases).
  - **The card's approvals criterion:** environment A's pending request is answered on both mounts for A, and is a 404 through environment B, with B's service the one asked.
  - **One resolution, one kernel:** a hostname-routed request for a cold environment never calls `resolveKernel` to learn the id, and the kernel manager builds exactly that one environment once.
  - **Single kernel (the card's second hard criterion):** with no `kernel-manager` and no `kernel-resolver`, every door on both mounts is answered by the one kernel's occupant (14 cases).
- **Updated** `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts` (8). Each provider row now says whether it is host- or environment-scoped.
  - The slot-identity pin checks an environment-scoped provider against the environment kernel's occupant for `'env_1'`, and against the host's for no id and for `'platform'`.
  - The asked-slots pin records the five slots asked on the environment kernel.
  - A new describe pins the single-kernel reading per provider: for `'env_1'`, `undefined` and `'platform'`, each of the five resolves `ctx.getService(slot)` and makes exactly that one call.

## Acceptance notes

- **Changed answer, analytics only.** An environment whose kernel carries no analytics service, or whose kernel cannot be acquired, now gets the route's 501 where it used to get an answer from the host's service.
- **Faults keep their existing route answers.** A provider rejection (a kernel that cannot be acquired, a factory that threw) is caught by each route's existing `resolveService` catch, as before, so it answers that door's "not configured" shape (501, `{ data: [] }` or the empty record page part) rather than a 5xx. That is the routes' pre-existing contract and is not changed here. A wedged environment fails first in `resolveExecCtx` on these doors.
- **Scope.** The plugin's other provider seams (auth, objectql, i18n, settings, metadata, security, tenancy, endpoint match) are outside this card and are unchanged.
- **Cloud's re-read** of `areq_bcb78e81` on staging under cloud#3305 1f follows a pin round that carries this, and is cloud's work, not this PR's.

## Verification

- Full `@objectstack/rest` suite under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`: 385 files, 7,237 passed, 332 skipped, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck` over `tsconfig.test.json`): green, 0 errors, nothing held in the debt ledger.
- eslint on all nine touched source and test files: clean.
- The 60 commands `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derives for this diff, each run with its exit code recorded, reconciled by `dispatch-gates --ran`: 59 exit 0, 1 not measured.
  - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`): it reads every package's built `dist/`, and this worktree built only the `@objectstack/rest` closure. CI's whole-tree build runs it.
  - `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` first exited 3 because this clone is shallow and its pinned fixture commit was missing; after fetching that commit it passed (48 cases).
  - The text gates (closing-keyword parity, comment-mask adoption and corpus, issue citations, drift comment, affected docs, changeset no-major and empty-changeset, ADR-0087 registration, nul bytes), `check:slot-lookup` and `check:route-envelope` were re-run on the final head `f1334056`: all exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`: no path-derived tier mandate; 861 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold.

<details>
<summary>Ablation: the hosted-shape test against the base provider and route sources</summary>

With `rest-api-plugin.ts`, the five route modules and `rest-server.ts` restored to `73a3ef9f` and the new test file kept, the hosted describe reads **39 failed, 5 passed (44)**.

- The 5 that pass are the four analytics cases with the environment present (the route already read the environment's kernel first) and the cold-build case.
- The four analytics `env_bare` cases fail: the base route answered them from the host's service.
- Every approvals, sharing, sharing-rule, email and record page case fails.

With the fix the same file reads 58 passed (58). The single-kernel pins (the new describe and the updated slot-lookup file) pass on both trees, 15 run in the base-source run, which is the "unchanged" half.

</details>
